question: An internal reporting dashboard is used by 40 employees, behind login, for hours a day. Which attribute ranking fits best?
options: SEO first, then infrastructure cost
First paint under 500 ms at any cost
Team autonomy first, so each chart is a micro-frontend
Maintainability and time to market first; SEO is irrelevant and first-load cost is amortized over long sessions
explanation: Rank attributes for the product at hand. Behind login there is nothing to index, and a SPA served from a CDN is cheap and simple.

question: What does a team buy and what does it pay when it moves public product pages from a client-rendered SPA to SSR on every request?
options: Buys lower hosting cost, pays with SEO
Buys team autonomy, pays with performance
Buys SEO and faster first content, pays with server compute, operational complexity and hydration work on the client
Nothing changes, SSR and SPA have the same trade-offs
explanation: The HTML now contains real content, but every request runs React on a server that must be operated and paid for.

question: A documentation site with 20,000 pages takes 40 minutes to build with SSG, and typo fixes wait for the full build. Which attribute is being paid?
options: SEO
Freshness and build time (time to publish) in exchange for the fastest, cheapest delivery
Team autonomy
Accessibility
explanation: SSG trades freshness and build cost for speed and cheap hosting. ISR or on-demand revalidation can rebalance the trade.

question: Product says the new marketplace must be "fast, SEO friendly, cheap, infinitely scalable and shippable by any team at any time". What is the most useful next step?
options: Ask for a ranking of these attributes for the first release, because the options trade them against each other
Adopt micro-frontends and SSR to cover everything
Pick the most popular framework
Ignore the requirements and build a SPA
explanation: No option maximizes every attribute. A ranking makes the trade-offs explicit and lets the team pick and document a choice.

question: Moving business rules out of components into a pure domain module behind interfaces mainly improves which attribute, at what cost?
options: SEO, at the cost of performance
Infrastructure cost, at the cost of SEO
First-load performance, at the cost of maintainability
Testability and framework independence, at the cost of more files and indirection
explanation: Pure functions and ports are easy to test without React or a network, but the extra layer must earn its place through real business complexity.

question: Two options satisfy the top-ranked attributes equally well. Which tie-breaker does the lesson recommend?
options: The newest technology
The option with more GitHub stars
The option that is cheaper to reverse
The option with the most layers, for future flexibility
explanation: Reversible decisions keep options open at low cost. Extra layers "for the future" are a cost paid now for a benefit that may never come.
